data.name: Guide_AccelCause
data.value: Pointer acceleration is on in the phone, so fast mouse movements make the return to the laptop late.

data.name: Guide_AccelManual
data.value: To change it yourself, turn off pointer acceleration on the phone under Settings → General management → Mouse and trackpad (the name may differ by device).

data.name: Guide_NoDevice_Cause
data.value: No phone is connected, or the cable only charges.

data.name: Guide_NoDevice_Steps
data.value: Unplug the cable and plug it into the phone and the laptop again. Use a cable that can transfer data (charge-only cables do not show the phone). Try another USB port on the laptop.

data.name: Guide_DebuggingOff_Cause
data.value: The phone is visible over USB, but USB debugging is off.

data.name: Guide_DebuggingOff_Steps
data.value: On the phone, open Settings → About phone → Software information and tap Build number 7 times to turn on Developer options. Open Settings → Developer options and turn on USB debugging. If you cannot turn it on, open Settings → Security and privacy → Auto Blocker and turn it off. If it still does not work, install the Samsung USB driver on the laptop.

data.name: Guide_Unauthorized_Cause
data.value: The phone has not allowed this laptop yet.

data.name: Guide_Unauthorized_Steps
data.value: Unlock the phone and look for the "Allow USB debugging?" prompt. Check "Always allow from this computer" and tap Allow. If no prompt appears, unplug the cable and plug it in again. If it still does not appear, open Settings → Developer options → Revoke USB debugging authorizations, then reconnect.

data.name: Guide_Offline_Cause
data.value: The connection to the phone is unstable.

data.name: Guide_Offline_Steps
data.value: Unplug the cable and plug it in again. Unlock the phone.

data.name: Guide_MultipleDevices_Cause
data.value: More than one Android device is connected, so PhoneEdge cannot tell which phone to use.

data.name: Guide_MultipleDevices_Steps
data.value: Connect only the phone you want to use and unplug the others.

data.name: Guide_AdbFailed_Cause
data.value: adb could not run. Another program's adb may conflict with it, or security software may be blocking it.

data.name: Guide_AdbFailed_Steps
data.value: Press Retry below. Close Android Studio, Smart Switch or another scrcpy if they are running, then try again. Check whether security software on this laptop is blocking adb.exe.

data.name: Guide_Server_Short
data.value: Phone input service failed to start

data.name: Guide_Server_Cause
data.value: The input service on the phone could not be started.

data.name: Guide_Server_Steps
data.value: Press Retry below. On the phone, check that Settings → Security and privacy → Auto Blocker is turned off. Restart the phone and reconnect the cable.

data.name: Menu_DisableDebugging
data.value: Turn off phone USB debugging on exit

data.name: Menu_DisableDebuggingHint
data.value: Banking and securities apps may refuse to run while USB debugging is on. PhoneEdge turns it off when it exits. To use PhoneEdge again, turn USB debugging back on in the phone's Developer options.

data.name: Companion_Confirm
data.value:
Install the PhoneEdge Companion app on the phone?
Many banking and securities apps refuse to run while USB debugging is on, but PhoneEdge needs it. The helper app turns USB debugging on when the phone is connected to a computer with a data cable and off when the cable is unplugged.
PhoneEdge installs it over USB and sets it up for you: it gives the app permission to change the USB debugging setting and excludes it from battery optimization. The app shows a permanent notification with the current state. You can uninstall it like any other app.

data.name: Companion_Done
data.value: The phone helper app is ready. It keeps a notification on the phone; if it stops after a while, set the app's battery usage to Unrestricted (see the README).

data.name: Companion_Failed
data.value: Could not install the phone helper app. Make sure the phone is unlocked and connected, then try again. The log file has the details.
